observation.visible_scene: Side (driver-side) view of a blue hatchback inside a crash-test hall, its front end already heavily crushed against a fixed silver-grey barrier on the right edge of the frame. An orange crash-test dummy sits in the driver's seat; a second, darker dummy/restraint is faintly visible in the rear. The background is a dim warehouse with vertical and diagonal metal beams and a concrete floor. Small bright debris particles hang in the air above the crumpled front throughout the clip.
visible_changes: The front crush zone deepens progressively: the hood, fender and A-pillar fold further inward toward the barrier, and the windshield shatters more extensively.
The front wheel is pushed rearward into the wheel arch, the tire visibly deforms and the rim rotates as the structure collapses.

The side body and door panel begin to buckle near the front hinge area; the lower side molding tilts slightly downward toward the front, indicating a small forward pitch of the cabin as the front collapses.
The dummy's head and torso move forward relative to the seat and toward the steering column over the segment.

A row of white circular tracking markers (a superimposed annotation, not a physical object) first appears near the dummy's head around mid-clip and accumulates into a horizontal trail across the window, recording the head's successive positions.
The suspended debris particles above the front continue to drift/settle slowly; the barrier and background remain fixed, so the apparent motion is the car deforming and pitching, not camera panning.
outside_clip_unknowns: The moment and speed of first contact (the crush is already well underway at t=0).
Whether the car fully stops, rebounds, or continues moving after t=3.2.
The dummy's final injury metrics and any airbag deployment not visible in these frames.
uncertain_details: Exact rear-wheel lift vs. ground contact is hard to confirm; the body's forward tilt is subtle.
The white dots are interpreted as an editing/overlay tracking graphic rather than physical debris; their precise meaning (head trajectory) is inferred from their placement.
Camera is treated as static based on the fixed barrier and beams, but a very slight shift cannot be fully excluded.
